content.value_statement: Unsafe user content can expose applications to policy and trust risks. This skill guides TypeScript integrations for Azure text, image, and blocklist moderation.
actual_capabilities: Configures the Azure REST client with an API key or DefaultAzureCredential.
Analyzes text across hate, sexual, violence, and self-harm categories.
Analyzes images from local Base64 content or Azure Blob URLs.
Creates, lists, updates, and deletes custom text blocklists.
Interprets four-level and eight-level severity outputs.
Builds a reusable TypeScript moderation helper with configurable thresholds.
limitations: Requires an Azure Content Safety resource, endpoint, credentials, and network access.
Provides integration guidance and examples, not a deployed moderation service.
Azure severity results still require application-specific policies and human review.
Example paths, blocklist names, thresholds, and error handling need production adaptation.

use_cases.title: Moderate Community Text
use_cases.description: Add harm-category checks and custom blocked terms before publishing comments or messages.

use_cases.title: Screen Uploaded Images
use_cases.description: Submit local files or blob URLs for category severity analysis before storage or display.

use_cases.title: Standardize Moderation Policies
use_cases.description: Create shared thresholds and blocklists for consistent decisions across TypeScript services.

prompt_templates.title: Install and Connect
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to install the Azure Content Safety packages and initialize the TypeScript REST client with environment variables.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Text
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a TypeScript example that analyzes text for all harm categories and reports each severity.

prompt_templates.title: Add Domain Blocklists
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a blocklist workflow that creates a list, adds terms, analyzes text, and handles matches.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Moderation Service
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production TypeScript moderation helper with category thresholds, blocklists, error handling, audit logging, and human review routing.

output_examples.input: Analyze a comment and block severity levels above two.
output_examples.output: A TypeScript workflow submits the comment, checks every harm category, and returns an allow decision with flagged categories.

output_examples.input: Moderate an uploaded image from disk.
output_examples.output: A guided example reads the image, converts it to Base64, submits it to Azure, and handles unexpected responses.

output: Create or update a named blocklist.
Analyze text with the blocklist enabled.
Report matched terms for policy handling.

best_practices: Keep Azure keys in environment variables or managed identity and never include them in prompts or logs.
Set category thresholds from documented policy and route uncertain cases to human review.
Handle unexpected API responses, empty results, unsupported files, and service failures explicitly.
anti_patterns: Do not treat one global severity threshold as a complete moderation policy.
Do not expose matched harmful text or credentials in unrestricted logs.
Do not allow content automatically when the moderation service fails.

faq.question: Which Azure package does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses the Azure REST package named @azure-rest/ai-content-safety with Azure authentication packages.

faq.question: Can it analyze both text and images?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples cover text, Base64 image content, and images referenced by blob URLs.

faq.question: Which harm categories are supported?
faq.answer: The documented categories are hate, sexual, violence, and self-harm.

faq.question: Does it support custom blocked terms?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to create blocklists, add items, analyze text, list entries, and delete lists.

faq.question: Can I use managed Azure credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes API key and DefaultAzureCredential initialization patterns.

faq.question: Does the skill decide my production policy?
faq.answer: No. Your team must define thresholds, review rules, logging controls, and failure behavior.
